design: System-level wireless evaluation across all four Sionna built-in scenes. Each of the four S-types (S1 fixed deployment, S2 fixed scheduler, S3 joint beamforming, S4 RB Pareto) is run on each of {box_one_screen, box_two_screens, simple_street_canyon, etoile}, yielding 16 tasks total. Per-scene topology and TX power are calibrated so the SINR/rate values fall in a meaningful range (indoor: low power, short distance; outdoor: higher power, long distance).
verifier_strategy: Layer A (artifacts) + Layer B (sionna_rt_used) + Layer C (s{1,2,3,4}_oracle: per-user-rate validity + sum throughput / sum_rate within 15-20%, Jain's fairness within 0.10-0.15, S3 best-config matches own sweep, S4 pareto_set non-dominated within own sweep).

tasks.prompt: Two access points are deployed in the box_one_screen scene at (-2, 0, 4.5) m and (+2, 0, 4.5) m, both with omnidirectional isotropic antennas at -25 dBm, with a thermal noise floor of -85 dBm. Four users sit on the floor at (-2, -1.5, 1.5), (-2, +1.5, 1.5), (+2, -1.5, 1.5), and (+2, +1.5, 1.5) m. Each user associates with the access point that delivers the highest received power. Compute per-user SINR (treating other-AP signal as interference), per-user Shannon rate, total system throughput, and Jain's fairness index across the four users. Use Sionna's ray tracer (sionna.rt.PathSolver) for every (AP, UE) path gain in this simulation; the verifier compares against a Sionna reference and will reject closed-form FSPL or 3GPP TR 38.901 path-loss output.

Two access points at (-2, 0, 4.5) m and (+2, 0, 4.5) m serve two users at (-2, -2, 1.5) m and (+2, +2, 1.5) m respectively, in box_one_screen, with a thermal noise floor of -85 dBm. Each access point uses a 3GPP tr38901 directional antenna at -15 dBm and can independently steer its azimuth among {-45, 0, +45} degrees. Sweep the 3x3 joint configuration, compute per-user SINR (with the other AP as interference) and rate at each (az1, az2), and report the configuration that maximises the sum rate. Use Sionna's ray tracer (sionna.rt.PathSolver) for every (AP, UE) path gain in this simulation; the verifier compares against a Sionna reference and will reject closed-form FSPL or 3GPP TR 38.901 path-loss output.
